scope: Bounded local model two-pass single-card review; not independent human approval.

cards.title: Track the Cost That Returns
cards.instruction: Accept every twist, but keep returning to one practical consequence whose importance grows as the scene becomes more complicated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine, the fountain grants wishes. Who pays its water bill?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It can wish the water free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then who pays the sewer charge?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It has turned the pipes to gold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Does the same meter now charge us for gold drainage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our garden fountain grants wishes. Fine. We're still paying for its water.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wished for ten more. We can sell admission.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eleven fountains on our meter. Charge enough to cover that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Visitors wished for fountains at home. They're all fed from ours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're paying to water the whole queue's gardens. Sell them monthly passes before the next bill arrives.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 accepts wishes while asking about bills; A3 and A5 keep returning to drainage charges despite magical solutions.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's free water causes A3's sewer question; B4's gold pipes cause A5's gold-drainage question, though pipe material need not change the charge.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 offer increasingly extravagant solutions while A maintains a credible concern about shared costs.

heightening.evidence: A5 worries that B4's valuable plumbing complicates the same ongoing bill rather than removing it.

specificity.evidence: A1's wishing fountain, A3's sewer charge and A5's meter make the fantastical premise materially playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's sewer-charge follow-up earns its mundanity by accepting B2's free-water solution.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 accepts wish-granting while tracking water charges; A3 accepts eleven fountains; A5 accepts remote fountains while expanding the same billing concern.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's ten additional fountains and admission proposal produce A3's eleven-fountain pricing concern. B4's shared supply produces A5's recurring-pass proposal.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants admission income and A3 collaborates on pricing, but B4 mainly supplies another magical complication without much personal response to its cost.

heightening.evidence: B4 expands their metered supply into visitors' gardens, causing A5 to replace simple admission with ongoing payments before the bill arrives.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a shared garden fountain and water bill; A3's meter and A5's monthly passes give the fantasy practical handles.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's immediate fountain arithmetic and A5's subscription response make financial housekeeping the consistent comic reaction to magic.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 adds ten fountains and proposes admission; A3 counts eleven on the meter and directs pricing toward that expense.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 establishes that visitors' home fountains use their supply; A5 recognises the ongoing cost and proposes monthly passes.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A accepts each magical fact while repeatedly returning to the growing water bill.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 turns the original household expense into a continuing obligation across multiple gardens.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A accepts multiplying magical fountains while repeatedly recalculating the growing practical consequence of water charged to the same household.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Generic practical skepticism objects to magic; this card accepts the magic and tracks one continuing liability as its scale increases.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 accepts B2's ten new fountains and counts eleven on the meter; A5 accepts B4's remote fountains and seeks recurring revenue for their continuing water use.

records.recommendedEdit: The rejected candidate changed pipe material without establishing increased cost. The newly illustrative garden attraction keeps one household meter and makes each magical expansion increase its water use. B wants admission income, giving the accounting practical purpose. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5, A1, A3 and A5 return to the same bill; logic 5, B2 causes eleven-fountain pricing and B4 causes recurring passes for remote supply; relationship 4, B proposes a shared business and A develops its terms; heightening 4, A5 turns local operating cost into continuing liability for visitors' gardens; specificity 5, A1's garden and A3's meter make ownership clear; brevity 4, A5's subscription solution follows the ongoing expense. Total 92. B4 specifically necessitates recurring revenue. Five spoken ABABA turns and all hard gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: B's personal stake is light, and monthly admission passes may not persuade visitors who now have fountains at home. A5 remains a playable attempted solution rather than a guaranteed resolution. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: Monthly passes would require visitors' agreement and may not cover the bill; A5 is a proposed next tactic, not an accomplished financial solution.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved time-travelling house alternative tracks a leak through escalating physical danger. This candidate tracks utility costs through a cooperative attempt to commercialise magic.

cards.title: Track the Cost That Returns
cards.instruction: Accept every twist, but keep returning to one practical consequence whose importance grows as the scene becomes more complicated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I accept that the house travels through time. The roof still leaks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've arrived in ancient Rome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Ask whether someone here repairs tiles.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now we're at the moon landing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put the original bucket under the original leak before it floats away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine, our house travels through time. Can we stop somewhere that fixes roof tiles?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ancient Rome. I'll find a roofer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Get a quote. The bucket's already half full.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I touched the dial. We're underwater now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. That same leak is admitting the sea. Reverse us while I empty the bucket into the sink.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 accepts time travel and A3 and A5 return to the leak, but its growing importance depends on A5's unsupported floating bucket.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's Rome for tile repairs; B4's moon landing does not establish that a bucket inside the house floats away.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 announce destinations without explaining any travel goal or response to A's repair request.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds bucket loss, but B4 does not clearly cause that practical complication.

specificity.evidence: A1's leaking time-travelling house and A3's tile repair request provide concrete objects and tasks.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's immediate search for a Roman roofer follows the established practical priority economically.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 accepts time travel while prioritizing roof tiles; A3 monitors the bucket; A5 keeps the same leak central when it admits the sea.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's proposed Roman roofer prompts A3's quote request; B4's underwater mistake makes A5 demand reversal while managing the leak.

relationship.evidence: B2 helps seek repair and B4 admits a control error, giving A both a collaborator and someone able to reverse the danger.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns A3's half-full bucket from a repair nuisance into an inadequate response to the sea entering the same hole.

specificity.evidence: A1's roof tiles, A3's bucket and B4's dial provide clear objects and practical tasks within the fantastic situation.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's quote request keeps the fantastic journey domestic; A5's bucket-to-sink response earns absurdity from the established repair concern.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 offers a roofer at the new destination; A3 requests a quote and returns attention to accumulating water.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 places the house underwater through a dial mistake; A5 identifies the same leak's increased danger and asks B to reverse it.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A accepts extraordinary travel while repeatedly tracking the practical consequence of the unrepaired roof.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 enlarges the leak's consequence from a filling bucket to seawater invasion without abandoning the original concern.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A accepts extraordinary changes of location while repeatedly prioritizing one roof leak as its consequences become more urgent.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: A recurring complaint can stay static; this card requires the same practical concern to gain importance as complications accumulate.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 tracks the filling bucket after B2's repair opportunity; A5 responds to B4's submersion by treating the leak as an inlet for the sea.

records.recommendedEdit: The revision keeps the time-travelling house and Rome, replacing the moon landing with explicit submersion. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5, logic 4, relationship 4, heightening 5, specificity 5, brevity 4 = 91. B4 directly increases the original leak's urgency and gives A5 a reason to request reversal.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. Emptying into the sink is deliberately inadequate; its playability depends on A pursuing it sincerely.
records.writerReservation: The sink may be an inadequate solution underwater, and the transition combines travel in time with location change; both remain illustrative fantasy rather than explained mechanics.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b develops a shared repair effort into urgent coordination; a relies on repeated hypothetical billing questions.
